_comment: TODO-SYSOP: placeholder fortunes drafted for PIZON BBS. Edit freely; one string per fortune, keep each under ~200 characters.
fortunes: It is certain. The spirits double-checked the checksum.
Without a doubt. Even the parity bit agrees.
Yes. Now hang up before your mom picks up the extension.
Most likely. Odds improve if you stop downloading during dinner.
Outlook good. Outlook Express, less so.
Signs point to yes. They also point to the snack aisle.
Yes, but read the README.TXT first. Nobody reads the README.TXT.
The answer is yes, compressed with PKZIP. Unzip carefully.
Ask again after the carrier settles. Line noise detected.
Reply hazy. Somebody picked up the phone mid-transfer.
Cannot predict now. The Oracle is busy uploading.
Concentrate and ask again. Preferably at 2400 baud or better.
Better not tell you now. The SysOp is reading over my shoulder.
Don't count on it. Don't count on your hard drive either; back it up.
My reply is no. My other reply is also no.
Very doubtful. About as likely as a clean ZMODEM transfer during a thunderstorm.
No. But the SysOp believes in you anyway.
The spirits say: it depends on your IRQ settings.
Yes, if you can find the right disk. It is always disk 7 of 9.
A great opportunity awaits behind a 'Press any key to continue'.
You will soon receive an unexpected message. Check your mail before the SysOp does.
The future is bright, like a CRT at full contrast. Turn it down a little.
Beware of strangers offering free warez. They bring viruses and regret.
Your patience will be rewarded, at roughly 1.8 kilobytes per second.
Today is a good day to defragment something. Your hard drive, or your life.
The answer you seek lies in the file areas. Probably in a file called ANSWER.ZIP.
You will be remembered fondly in the message bases.
A friend will soon call. Unfortunately, so will a telemarketer, mid-download.
Fortune favors those who type in lowercase. Stop shouting.
Your hard work is about to pay off. Save your game first.
Trust the process. And the power strip. Mostly the power strip.
The spirits sense great potential and a dusty keyboard.
Something you lost will turn up, probably in C:\TEMP.
You are about to learn something new. The hard way, via a Guru Meditation.
Love is in the air. So is the hum of a 14.4k modem.
The stars align. So do your columns, finally.
Your next idea is worth sharing. Post it to the message board.
Wealth comes to those who wait. The SysOp is still waiting.
Take the risk. Worst case, you reboot.
A long journey begins with a single keystroke. Try Enter.
Your aura reads 256 colors, all of them bright.
The Oracle sees a door in your future. Possibly literally; this is a BBS.
Someone admires your handle. Choose your next one wisely.
Good things are buffering. Do not unplug the modem.
The answer is 42. The question was compressed too hard.
Not today. Tomorrow, maybe, once the long-distance rates drop after 11 PM.
Yes, but only on weekends and after the SysOp's bedtime.
Your path is clear, unlike this phone line.
Kindness returns to you, like a bounced packet.
The spirits say ask a better question. Perhaps one with fewer typos.
In the end, every file finishes downloading. Hold on.
You will soon upgrade. Your RAM, your mood, or both.
Your luck is changing. Your password should too.
A small risk brings a large reward. A large risk brings a call from the phone company.
The Oracle is unsure, and frankly a little sleepy.
Yes. The spirits have spoken. The spirits would like a snack now.
Look closer at what is already in front of you. Like the menu. Press a key.
Your question has been forwarded to the SysOp, who laughed and then said yes.
Absolutely. Write it in the guestbook so it becomes official.
The spirits say: NO CARRIER. Ask again.
Follow your curiosity. It has better taste than your download ratio.
